transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your busy day. I'm just here because... well, my pastor thought it would be a good idea for me to come talk to someone. I've just been a little, oh, I don't know, distracted maybe? It's really nothing too terrible, I promise. 

I help out a lot at our church, you see, especially with the potlucks. I always try to be a good helper for everyone. But lately, I've been doing some... well, some silly things, I suppose. I feel a bit ashamed even saying it out loud, because I don't want people to think poorly of me. But sometimes I'll just be standing by the food table, holding the serving spoon right up in the air, and I just... I don't move. I just kind of freeze there. Or I'll catch myself folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over and over again, right while folks are standing there waiting on me to hand them one. 

I don't mean to be a bother to anyone, and I feel just awful about holding up the line. Am I explaining that okay for you, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
When you find yourself freezing or repeating the folding, is there a disturbing thought or fear that comes into your mind right before it happens?

Oh, my... no, Doctor. I don't think so. I hope that's an alright answer. 

I don't have any scary thoughts or... or worries right before it happens. It's more like... well, my mind just sort of goes blank, I suppose. Just quiet. I'm so sorry if that's not very helpful for your notes. I really am trying to give you the best answers I can. I just don't remember feeling afraid or anything like that. Is it okay that I don't have a thought like that to tell you about?
Right before you freeze or repeat the folding, do you feel like you have to keep going until it feels 'just right'?

Oh, goodness... no, sir. I don't think it's like that. I'm really not trying to be fussy or make them perfect, I promise. I know some of the ladies at the church get real particular about how the table looks, but... well, for me, I just sort of lose my place, I guess. 

It's not a feeling of needing it to be just right. I just keep doing it without really meaning to. I hope it's alright that I don't have that feeling you're asking about. Am I doing okay answering your questions, Doctor? I just want to be as helpful as I can be for you.
Do you ever make sudden movements or sounds that happen on their own, like blinking, shoulder shrugging, or clearing your throat?

Oh, dear... no, I don't believe so. I hope I'm not disappointing you with all these 'no' answers, Doctor. 

I try very hard to be polite and, well, proper, especially at church. I don't think I make any sudden noises or jerks like that. I mean, sometimes my joints are a little stiff at my age, but I don't have any twitches or anything that I can't control. I'm so sorry if that's not what you were looking for. Is it helpful at all that I don't have those things happening? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your evaluation.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out OCD (F42) features of intrusive fear/urges and 'just right' compulsion, and ruled out tic disorder (F44.5) due to absence of involuntary sudden movements/sounds. Presentation remains most consistent with dependent personality traits/disorder code F60.7 given pervasive appeasement, excessive deference, and fear of displeasing others.
